decisions.note: Locator 47:201272 is verified as JP 先頭プライド. 'Kiêu hãnh dẫn đầu' preserves the pride-in-leading idea in a compact Vietnamese skill title.
Locator 47:201271 is verified as JP トップランナー. 'Người dẫn đầu' is the direct natural Vietnamese concept and remains distinct from 先頭プライド.

Locator 47:107802211 is verified as JP シルフ・スピリット. The title contains the mythological/loanword element シルフ; defer until the project chooses a consistent Romanization versus Vietnamese treatment for such fantasy terms.
Locator 47:202411 is verified as JP 風雲の志. The compact literary phrase admits several Vietnamese registers; defer rather than locking an opaque Hán-Việt calque or an over-explicit paraphrase.
Locator 47:107801111 is verified as JP ウインドシアー (wind shear). 'Gió đứt' is the established Vietnamese aviation-meteorology term for wind shear, so it is preferable to a Chinese calque.
Locator 47:107802111 is verified as JP 塵旋風となりて. The Chinese bridge uses a different idiom; 'Hóa thành lốc bụi' is locked directly from the Japanese dust-whirlwind image.

Locator 47:104402111 is a character-specific evolution title, but its exact JP display wording was not sufficiently verified in the checked evidence. Do not construct a canonical fantasy title from the Chinese semantic bridge.

Locator 47:103101211 is verified as JP 荒ぶる風神. Although the wind-god image is clear, Vietnamese choices differ between a compact Sino-Vietnamese deity title and a more natural descriptive phrase; defer for character/title style consistency.
Locator 47:105301111 is verified as JP 風紀の登龍門. 登龍門 is an idiom/metaphor and 風紀 is character-specific disciplinary wording; several Vietnamese formulations are possible, so defer.
Locator 47:105101111 is verified as JP 風花疾走. The compact poetic compound 風花 is image-rich and does not have one clearly dominant natural Vietnamese title; defer.
Locator 47:104702211 is a literary/character-flavor evolution title. Exact JP wording and its intended classical allusion were not sufficiently verified to support one canonical Vietnamese rendering.
Locator 47:101702211 is a literary evolution title. The four-character Chinese bridge is not sufficient authority for the exact Japanese source nuance, so defer instead of freezing a literary calque.
Locator 47:203321 is verified as JP 舞い降りる翼. Natural Vietnamese options such as 'đôi cánh hạ xuống' or more poetic variants differ markedly in rhythm; defer for title-style review.
Locator 47:110991 is verified as JP とびだせ☆ポッピングシェル. The playful imperative, ☆, and katakana loanword phrase need character-aware stylization; do not back-translate the Chinese title literally.
Locator 47:202352 is verified as JP 土煙, a cloud of dust kicked up from the ground. 'Bụi mù' is a concise natural Vietnamese skill title for that image.
Locator 47:110701111 uses the Latin title 'Breakaway Star' directly in JP data. Preserve the original title instead of translating the Chinese semantic localization.

Locator 47:203022 is verified as JP 風切り. In the racing/motion context, 'Rẽ gió' is a concise natural Vietnamese rendering of cutting through the wind and avoids relying on the Chinese one-word bridge.
Locator 47:108201211 uses the Latin title 'Enjoy the Flight' directly in JP data. Preserve the original spelling rather than translating back from the Chinese semantic title.
Locator 47:202901 is verified as JP 飛翔脚. Literal Hán-Việt would sound unnatural while freer choices such as a 'soaring stride' change the compact martial-technique flavor; defer.
